tables.how: The Controller's payment file for payees it marks as nonprofit, summed by payee, department, fiscal year, contract and purchasing rule. A row is kept when the rule's wording says no bid, not bid, emergency, sole source or no other source, or names one of the standing waivers ('Core Initiatives Addressing Homelessness...', 'Projects Addressing Homelessness', 'Behavioral Health and Residential Care Contracts by DPH'), for fiscal 2019 to 2026; the University of California is left out as a public body. 3,896 rows to 706 payees add up to $2,013,727,763: emergency $851,977,677, standing waivers $711,785,116, sole source $379,218,133, other not-bid rules $70,746,838. The six largest payees received $859,093,743 (43%): Tenderloin Housing Clinic Inc $283.6 million; Episcopal Community Svcs Of S F Inc $207.5 million; Five Keys Schools And Programs $134.2 million; Urban Alchemy $80.0 million; Healthright 360 $76.9 million; Brilliant Corners $76.8 million. The year is the fiscal year the file lists a payment under, as in the analysis the case quotes.
tables.limits: On the rules here: the Board passed the waivers in public, emergency purchasing is allowed in a declared emergency, and a sole-source award needs a written reason. A payment under a no-bid rule says nothing about price or quality. The rule is the one staff keyed on the payment, and an old wording can stay on a contract after the reason for it has changed. The rule 'Prop Q authority with bid' ($3,998,801) is counted here because the analysis sorts every Prop Q wording as not bid. For some lines the file's fiscal year is later than the year the payment was issued.
